name: AND of a copied bit
summary: Two parallel wires between a Z-spider and an H-box can be replaced by a single wire.
description:
If a Z-spider and an H-box are connected by two parallel wires, one of them can be removed. Here this is shown for an arity-3 H-box and an arity-3 Z-spider, where the result is a single arity-2 H-box. Since the Z-spider copies computational basis states, this expresses that $x \wedge x = x$: copying a bit and then taking the AND of the two copies gives back the original bit.

Although it looks simple, this rule is surprisingly hard to derive in the phase-free ZH-calculus: the phase-free paper derives it using the [AND rule](../zh-and-rule/). The 2021 completeness paper shows that, together with [Z(π) copying through an H-box](../zh-h-box-z-pi-copy/), it can replace the [ortho rule](../zh-ortho/) in the axiomatisation. More generally, the same holds for H-boxes with any label and any number of other legs on the Z-spider and the H-box.
notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
